summary: ClassifyDesign's heuristic pass skips the RCT tier when every randomisation signal sits in a sentence that credits another study — a host trial the participants came from. The phrase must be followed by a/an/the, and the title must not itself say randomised.
reason: A nested study names the trial it sat inside, and the heuristics cannot tell whose design they just read: one such phrase promoted a case-control study eight tiers to the apex of the pyramid. Three narrowings are load-bearing and must survive a regeneration — the determiner, which separates a host trial from a work saying 'this randomised trial' about itself; the sentence scoping, so an abstract that names a host AND describes its own randomisation keeps the second; and the title exception, so a work stating its own design in the title is never overruled.
validated_outcome: Zero matches across the 246 works in testdata/corpora, and no design or verdict change on any corpus. Six tests, each verified by mutation: removing the determiner, the sentence scoping, the title exception, or the tier skip each fails a different one, and forcing the guard always-on fails all three RCT-keeping tests. Wider rules were measured and rejected — giving the title priority over title+abstract changes 3 works, over the publication type 4, all in the wrong direction, since titles routinely name two designs and the pyramid order already picks correctly.
